vietnam.overview: Modest, beginner-friendly beach breaks line Vietnam's central and southern coasts, most notably at My Khe in Da Nang and Back Beach in Vung Tau. The surf season runs from autumn through spring, driven by the northeast monsoon, providing fun, accessible waves for learners and longboarders.

punta-cana.overview: Consistent reef breaks cluster along the north coast of the Dominican Republic, centered around Playa Encuentro. Winter north swells light up expert reefs like Destroyers and Coco Pipe, while beginners find forgiving inside sections and beach breaks. The water is 77-84 F, so no wetsuit is needed.

snowdonia.overview: Rugged, consistent beach and reef breaks line the Gower Peninsula and Pembrokeshire coast of Wales. Llangennith provides miles of beginner-friendly sandy peaks, while Freshwater West offers heavier waves for advanced surfers. The best swells arrive in autumn and winter.

palau.overview: Remote, uncrowded reef breaks in Palau suit intermediate and expert surfers during the northern hemisphere winter. The main waves are Santa Maria at Angaur and West Passage near Babeldaob, both requiring a boat trip to reach. There is little to no surf industry here, so visitors must bring their own shortboards and navigate shallow reefs.

papua-new-guinea.overview: Remote, uncrowded point breaks like Lido Right suit intermediate and advanced surfers in Papua New Guinea. The season runs from November to April when North Pacific swells reach the islands. Access often requires staying at a surf camp and paying reef fees to local landowners, and the water is 81-86 F so no wetsuit is needed.

guatemala.overview: Consistent, punchy beach breaks line Guatemala's Pacific coast, centered around the black sands of El Paredon and Sipacate. It suits beginners in the dry season and experienced surfers when the larger south swells arrive. The water is a warm 82-86 F year-round, so no wetsuit is needed.

bordeaux.overview: Miles of punchy beach breaks line the Gironde coast about an hour west of Bordeaux, most notably at Lacanau-Océan. It suits all levels in summer when waves are smaller and surf schools operate, but autumn brings the best conditions for experienced surfers with solid Atlantic swells and offshore winds.

galapagos.overview: Powerful, hollow reef breaks, primarily on San Cristóbal, suit intermediate and expert surfers in the Galápagos Islands. North swells light up signature spots like Punta Carola and El Cañón from November to April. Access often requires a boat and local permits, and the shallow volcanic reefs demand respect.

edinburgh.overview: Cold, consistent winter surf and mellow summer waves can be found on the North Sea coast east of Edinburgh. Belhaven Bay in Dunbar, 45 minutes away, is a beginner-friendly beach break with local surf schools. An hour away, Pease Bay provides a punchier reef and beach break for intermediate and advanced surfers.

dubai.overview: Modest, short-period beach breaks form at Sunset Beach in Dubai when winter Shamal winds push swell into the Persian Gulf. It suits beginners and longboarders, but the waves are small and inconsistent, with flat spells dominating the summer months.

borneo.overview: Modest, seasonal surfing can be found at the northern tip of Sabah in Malaysian Borneo, near Kudat, about three hours from Kota Kinabalu. The sandy beach breaks at Kalampunian Beach suit beginners and longboarders, working only during the northeast monsoon. It is a fun, tropical wave rather than a destination for experienced surfers.

provence.overview: Modest, wind-driven surf rolls onto the Mediterranean coast of Provence during the winter months, primarily around Marseille and Martigues. Short-period waves at breaks like Sausset-les-Pins and Épluchure suit beginners and intermediates when the Mistral wind blows, but the region is flat for much of the summer.

azores.overview: Uncrowded beach breaks and powerful reef setups line the rugged basalt coastline of the Azores, anchored by the consistent beach break at Santa Barbara on Sao Miguel. It suits all levels depending on the swell, with the most reliable waves arriving from September to April.

falklands.overview: Raw, cold-water surfing suits hardy, experienced surfers in the Falkland Islands, mainly at Surf Bay near Stanley. Swell is consistent year-round, but brutal winds and freezing water make it for the dedicated. There are no surf schools or rentals, so bring all your own gear.

okinawa.overview: Subtropical reef breaks line Okinawa, most notably Sunabe Seawall, which suits intermediate to advanced surfers. The waves work best during winter swells from October to March and summer typhoon swells, breaking over shallow coral that requires surfing around high tide.

puerto-rico.overview: Warm water and consistent winter reef breaks define Puerto Rico's west coast around Rincón. Domes is a fun right-hand point for intermediates, while Tres Palmas is an expert-only big wave reef that works only a few days a year. The main season runs from November to April when North Atlantic swells hit the island.

rio.overview: Consistent beach breaks and the famous left-hand point at Arpoador define the surf in Rio de Janeiro. Barra da Tijuca provides beginner-friendly peaks, while Arpoador and Macumba suit intermediate to advanced surfers. The best swells arrive in winter, though waves break year-round.

sydney.overview: Sydney's consistent, accessible beach breaks like Bondi and Manly suit all levels. Beginners find plentiful surf schools and gentle waves, while experienced surfers can hunt down punchier peaks at Maroubra or Cronulla. The surf works year-round, peaking in autumn and winter with larger swells.

st-andrews-fife.overview: St Andrews' modest, cold-water beach breaks, like East Sands, pick up North Sea swells. It suits intermediate surfers willing to brave the chill, working best from autumn through winter. There are few rentals, so visitors must bring their own gear.

mallorca.overview: Modest, wind-driven Mediterranean surf arrives on Mallorca during the winter months. Beginners can learn on the sandy stretches of Playa de Muro, while intermediates head to the reef at Son Serra de Marina or the beach break at Cala Ratjada when storms push swell to the north and east coasts.

maldives.overview: World-class reef breaks like Cokes and Chickens draw intermediate to expert surfers to the Maldives. Swells arrive from the south during the monsoon season, creating long, peeling waves over shallow coral. Access to most breaks requires a boat charter or staying at a specific resort.

hongkong.overview: Hong Kong's modest, beginner-friendly beach breaks are driven by the winter northeast monsoon. Big Wave Bay and Shek O are accessible spots for learners, while Tai Long Wan provides intermediate waves in a more remote setting reached by a hike or boat. Expect small 1-3 ft waves most days, with larger surf only during summer typhoons.

kerala.overview: Kerala's modest, warm-water waves suit beginners and intermediates, centered around the beach and point breaks of Varkala and Kovalam. The best conditions run from October to April when the Arabian Sea is clean and manageable, while the summer monsoon brings blown-out, rough seas.

nyc.overview: Rockaway Beach's accessible beach breaks, right in the city, suit beginners and intermediates. The best waves arrive with late summer hurricane swells and winter storms, producing 1-4 ft surf that can reach 6-8 ft on big days. Expect crowded lineups and designated surf zones during the summer months.

nova-scotia.overview: Consistent beach breaks at Lawrencetown Beach near Halifax suit beginners in summer and intermediates to experts during fall hurricane swells. The water is cold year-round (39-64 F, 5/4 mm hooded wetsuit most of the year), with strong rips on bigger days.

charleston-savannah.overview: Modest, sandy beach breaks suited for beginners and longboarders line Folly Beach in South Carolina and Tybee Island in Georgia. The Washout at Folly Beach is the most consistent spot, working best from September to December when fall swells arrive. Waves are typically 1 to 3 feet, and summer brings flat spells and daytime surfing restrictions.

cape-cod-islands.overview: Shifting sandbars on the outer beaches of Cape Cod pick up Atlantic swells, best suited for longboards and funboards on typical days. Hurricane swells in late summer and fall bring the best waves for experienced surfers. Great white sharks are a documented hazard here.

nicaragua.overview: Consistent year-round surf, famous for offshore winds and warm water, runs along Nicaragua's Pacific coast. Popoyo is a powerful reef break for intermediate to expert surfers, while Playa Maderas provides forgiving beach break peaks for beginners.

rome.overview: Real Mediterranean surf can be found on Rome's nearby coast, centered around Santa Marinella and the Banzai reef break, about an hour northwest of the city. Winter brings the most consistent windswell for intermediates and experts, while sandy beaches at Ostia provide gentle waves for beginners when conditions align.

redwood.overview: Heavy, cold-water beach breaks for intermediate and expert surfers line Crescent Beach and the surrounding Humboldt County coast. Winter swells from October to April bring powerful waves, but the environment is rugged, with strong rips, logs in the lineup, and documented great white sharks. The water is 48-57 F year-round, requiring a 5/4 mm hooded wetsuit with boots and gloves.

monterey-big-sur.overview: Classic cold-water point breaks line Monterey Bay and the surrounding coast. Steamer Lane provides heavy right-handers for experts, while Capitola and Pleasure Point offer mellow waves for beginners and intermediates. Winter brings the biggest swells, but smaller summer waves keep the longboard spots working year-round.

athens.overview: The Athenian Riviera offers a modest, storm-driven surf scene just south of the city. Beach breaks like Vouliagmeni and Varkiza occasionally produce 1-3 ft waves for beginners during winter storms. It is flat most of the year, leaving little for experienced surfers.

amsterdam.overview: The North Sea coast is about a 45-minute train ride from Amsterdam, with real cold-water surfing at beach breaks like Zandvoort and Wijk aan Zee. It relies on short-period wind swell, making it messy but fun for dedicated locals and beginners. Autumn brings the most consistent waves, while summer is often flat.

vancouver-island.overview: Tofino on Vancouver Island is Canada's surf capital, where consistent beach breaks sit against a rugged, forested coastline. Cox Bay handles larger swells for experienced surfers, while Chesterman Beach and Long Beach provide gentler waves for beginners. The water is cold year-round (46-60 F, 4/3 mm wetsuit in summer, 5/4 mm hooded with boots and gloves in winter). Watch out for strong rips and drift logs in the surf.

southeast-alaska.overview: Surfing in Southeast Alaska centers around Yakutat and Sitka, with remote, cold-water beach and point breaks for adventurous and experienced surfers. Swells are most consistent from autumn through spring, though access often requires a boat or a four-wheel-drive vehicle from town.

cornwall.overview: Cornwall is the center of English surfing, with consistent beach breaks like Fistral and Polzeath for beginners and intermediates, alongside heavy reefs like Porthleven for experts. Autumn and winter bring the most powerful Atlantic swells, while summer offers smaller, gentler waves.

lofoten.overview: Unstad is a renowned Arctic beach break with cold, powerful waves for intermediate and expert surfers. The best swells arrive from September to April, though winter brings extreme cold and very short daylight hours.

sicily.overview: Sicily gets real Mediterranean windswell in winter, with a mix of beach breaks for beginners near Palermo and rocky points like Kamikaze near Cefalù for experienced surfers. It is a quiet, low-key scene that relies on storms, so consistency is low compared to ocean coasts. Summer is flat.

ireland.overview: Ireland's rugged west coast catches powerful North Atlantic swells, which feed world-class heavy reefs for experts and consistent beach breaks for learners. Bundoran in County Donegal is the surf capital, home to The Peak, a hollow A-frame reef break. Nearby Mullaghmore Head produces massive, expert-only waves in winter. Beginners and intermediates find forgiving waves at beach breaks like Lahinch in County Clare and Strandhill in County Sligo.

fjords.overview: Surfing the Norwegian Fjords means cold water and dramatic scenery, with waves for beginners and intermediates at beach breaks like Hoddevik on the Stad Peninsula and the Jæren beaches. Swells are most consistent from late summer through autumn, though winter brings harsh conditions.

jamaica.overview: Modest but uncrowded reef breaks can be found primarily on Jamaica's east and north coasts. Boston Bay and Copa at Bull Bay suit beginners and intermediates, while Makka provides heavier sections for experts. The most consistent swells arrive from November to March.

komodo.overview: The south coast of Flores picks up Indian Ocean swell, resulting in empty, remote waves for adventurous experts. Access to the reef breaks requires a boat and local knowledge, with no surf schools or rentals available. It works best during the dry season.
